next_step: Finalize POC TTF validation and sign SOW; procurement to review pricing
notes: Intro call 2025-10-12: initial interest in reserved capacity for peak routing and last-mile ETA predictions.
Customer quote: "Predictable latency during peak loads is non-negotiable — we need 95th <= 50ms for small completion tasks."
Primary workload: mixed real-time chat (support agents), embeddings for route matching, and nightly reranking for fulfillment optimization.
POC ask: 4-week dedicated evaluation to validate throughput SLOs + cold-start behavior across 3 regions.
Throughput targets: sustained 150 req/s (avg cases), peak bursts to 600 req/s for 60-120s. Typical payload ~128 tokens per request; TTF (time-to-first-token) target <20ms for chat streams.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved GPUs if unit economics (tokens/sec/$) improves by >=30% vs hosted baseline.
Security: require VPC peering + customer-managed KMS; retention policy 90 days for logs, stricter for PII; SOC2 evidence requested before procurement sign-off.
SLA negotiation items: throughput guarantees for 99th percentile across committed GPU pool, credit schedule for missed latency SLOs, agreed maintenance windows (monthly 2hr).
Internal: AE/SE aligned on two-phase POC: Phase A (perf & autoscale behaviour), Phase B (failover + routing policy exercise).
POC environment provisioned 2026-01-05; synthetic load harness (k6 + custom tokenized clients) delivered 2026-01-18.
Load test run 1 (2026-02-01): sustained 160 req/s observed with 95th latency ~78ms; tail spikes during cold-starts. Action: evaluate warm-pool sizing + model variant routing.
Load test run 2 (2026-02-15): with 2 warm GPUs per AZ, sustained 155 req/s, 95th down to 48ms; peak 620 req/s for 90s ok with autoscale add-on nodes.
technical_requirements: Scale-up triggers: queued requests > 50 for >30s OR avg GPU util >85% for >60s OR 95th latency > SLO for 30s.
Scale-down triggers: node idle GPU util <20% AND queue length 0 for 5min; prefer gradual drain to prevent request loss.
Warm-pool policy: maintain 2 warm GPUs per AZ (configurable); warm nodes must keep model KV cache primed to reduce cold-start TTF.
Pre-warm steps: kernel preloads, precompile attention kernels, restore quantized model shards to GPU RAM before traffic shift.
Queueing behavior: request queue cap 200; priority lanes for low-latency chat traffic; best-effort batching for background reranking jobs.
Fallbacks: automatic route to smaller quantized model variant when queue > threshold or during emergency capacity shortage.
Continuous batching: combine small chats into micro-batches up to 8 tokens/window while preserving streaming semantics.
KV cache rehydration: snapshot/restore expected rewarm time <8s for active session caches — test during POC.
Burst capacity: ability to burst on preconfigured excess GPUs for 2-5min windows without impacting reserved baseline.
SLA items: define measurable SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latencies), throughput guarantees per reserved GPU pool, credits matrix for violations.
Operational hooks: tracing, token-level billing, per-model cost dashboards, and alerts tied to autoscale events.
Pod draining: graceful draining required; in-flight streaming requests must be proxied to fallback node if drain >30s.
Observability: require histograms of TTF, token generation rate, queue length, GPU temp/thermal throttling events.
Networking: deterministic egress lanes to avoid noisy-neighbor cross-talk; peering window constraints noted by infra team.
